sentences.text: Kelumapusaura is a saurolophine hadrosaur genus from the Late Cretaceous Allen Formation in Patagonia, Argentina.
The only known species, K. machi, is known from a bonebed containing multiple individuals.
The genus name combines the Mapudungun word for 'red earth' and the Greek word for 'lizard', while the species name 'machi' comes from the Mapuche word for 'shaman'.
Researchers estimate Kelumapusaura reached a length of 8 to 9 meters.
Rozadilla and colleagues named the genus in 2022, placing it within a clade of exclusively South American saurolophines.
Kelumapusaura belongs to the superfamily Hadrosauroidea, the family Hadrosauridae, and the tribe Kritosaurini.

A new South American clade containing Kelumapusaura is tentatively placed between Kritosaurini, supported by features like a subhorizontal crest on the ilium and a twisted distal end of the postacetabular process.

Kelumapusaura lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately between 73 and 69 million years ago, spanning the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages. Fossils were found in Late Cretaceous rocks of the Allen Formation in Patagonia, Argentina.
The Allen Formation also yielded fossils of titanosaurs, abelisaurids, dromaeosaurids, and alvarezsaurids.
The fossil record indicates a time range from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
It is debated how well the history of hadrosaurids on Gondwana is understood, with new discoveries potentially altering current views on their taxonomy and phylogenetic relationships.
